findings.description: CON-SUP-107 and SYS-SUP-014 do not define the program-code integrity method or reference value, so the check cannot be reproduced.
findings.requested_change: Define the program-code integrity method and reference value once the source decision is available.

findings.description: Failure of the start-up program-code check cannot be determined until its method and reference value are defined.
findings.requested_change: Define the conditions that constitute failure using the agreed integrity method and reference value.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-018 specifies segment size and frequency but not how a segment is checked or judged intact.
findings.requested_change: Define the run-time segment-check method and reference value once decided.

findings.description: Failure of a run-time program-code segment check cannot be determined until the check method and reference value are defined.
findings.requested_change: Define the conditions that constitute a failed segment check using the agreed method and reference value.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 and SYS-SUP-026 do not resolve whether the latch applies at the third fault or after the third supervisor reset.
findings.requested_change: Clarify the event that triggers the latch after the source owner resolves the sequence.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 permits a task name, CODE or CONFIG as the report entity but does not define the entity for watchdog-reset fault code 8.
findings.requested_change: Specify the entity for watchdog-reset reports after the source owner decides it.

findings.description: Neither SYS-SUP-037 nor CON-SUP-113 defines the permitted values and meanings of the returned state field.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the permitted state values and their meanings.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-004 requires detection when execution has not completed at the limit while permitting completion at that instant. CON-SUP-103 calls an execution longer than the limit an overrun and specifies detection at expiry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the equality boundary and detection instant with the source owner, then express a consistent rule.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC polynomial but not the remaining parameters and data-range details needed to reproduce the configuration CRC.
findings.requested_change: Specify the complete CRC parameters, covered data and stored reference representation after the source decision.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-038 requires eight reports for every GET FAULTS request, including when fewer exist; SYS-SUP-048 establishes an empty history after power restoration. CON-SUP-113 does not define that response.
findings.requested_change: Limit the eight-report obligation to the applicable case and obtain and specify the response when fewer reports exist.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-030 gives no deadline or precise event for driving the status signal high when its conditions hold.
findings.requested_change: Specify a verifiable timing bound or event after the source owner decides it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the reset cause to be readable by the service tool. SYS-SUP-032 transmits it at start-up, but the set defines no service request or response that retrieves it.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify a service-tool mechanism for reading the reset cause.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-033 detects watchdog-reset fault code 8, but SYS-SUP-022 through SYS-SUP-024 exclude it from the specified safe-state and recovery responses.
findings.requested_change: Resolve and specify the safe-state and recovery behavior for a detected watchdog-reset fault.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires transmission of the fault report after safe-state entry. SYS-SUP-024 imposes that ordering as part of the reset obligation but exempts latched safe states and start-up configuration faults; SYS-SUP-035 permits their reports before safe-state entry.
findings.requested_change: Specify the required report ordering for all applicable faults, including faults that latch the safe state.
